III. It is assumed for purposes of analysis that Tract II coal will be shipped through the Tract III handling plant; this assumption is consistent with the "low level" scenario. This will necessitate a haul road 4.5 miles in length across Sarpy Valley. All mined coal would be shipped by rail out of the state.
Acreage Disturbed - Approximate acreage to be disturbed by mining operations upon Tract II and III equals 32.2 acres and 17.5 acres respectively per million tons of coal. At the 19 million ton per year production level approximately 129 acres from Tract II and 263 acres from Tract III would be disturbed annually. These are average figures calculated on the basis of the total area underlain by coal. Tract II contains less two seam coal than Tract III which necessitates a greater amount of acreage being disturbed per million tons of coal.
Acreage Reclaimed - The amount of acreage reclaimed yearly is equal to the amount disturbed yearly with an approximate two year lag time. A previous section concerning reclamation of mined lands more fully describes reclamation and revegetation procedures.
Associated Facilities - The existing Tract III facilities occupy about 175 acres (an area of 360 acres has been approved for facilities).
In order to mine and deliver 4 million tons of coal annually from Tract II to the Tract III facilities a haul road of 4.5 miles covering approximately 136 acres will be required. Approximately 2.5 miles of powerline will be relocated and .2 miles of powerline will have to be constructed in order to facilitate mining operations upon Tract III. A portion of the existing county road upon Tract III would have to be relocated across previously mined areas as mining progresses (Map No. I-4).
